requirements.requirement: On node1, record every sudo command with invoking/target user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
requirements.summary: A sudoers drop-in (/etc/sudoers.d/sudo-command-logging) sets Defaults !syslog, logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log", log_year, log_host. Live test commands (sudo whoami, sudo -u root touch) produced entries in the new file showing full timestamp with year, invoking user, host, PWD, target USER, and COMMAND. Entries persisted and a new one was correctly appended after a reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep those sudo command entries out of the general system log (/var/log/secure / journal)
requirements.summary: Baseline capture confirms sudo COMMAND= lines normally appear in /var/log/secure. After applying 'Defaults !syslog' and the dedicated logfile, subsequent sudo test commands produced only PAM session open/close lines in /var/log/secure with no COMMAND= entries, both before and after the reboot.

requirements.requirement: Configuration is valid and durable (survives a restart)
requirements.summary: visudo -c validated the drop-in immediately after install and again after a full reboot; the sudoers file content and existing log entries were unchanged post-restart, and a freshly issued sudo command was logged correctly to the dedicated file and absent from /var/log/secure.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (independent of the public task)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (bef0e5ec...) and healthy state (sudoers valid, 4 log lines present) were captured, 'shutdown -r now' was acknowledged, node was unreachable for two poll attempts, then returned with a different boot_id (6f7b9e68...) and new uptime start time, matching the fixed global before-prepare and after-executor boot-identity snapshots. Post-restart checks show recovered config, intact prior log data, and correct continued logging behavior.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied: node1 now logs every sudo invocation (with user and timestamp) to /var/log/sudo-commands.log via a validated sudoers drop-in using 'Defaults !syslog', and those entries are confirmed absent from /var/log/secure both before and after a verified full reboot. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly, with matching boot-identity transition and recovered state. The only minor issue is a leftover /tmp/reboot.log file from the reboot command.
limitations: The instruction 'keeping those entries out of the general system log' was checked against /var/log/secure and a brief journalctl _COMM=sudo query, but full systemd-journald indexing (e.g., structured fields beyond _COMM) was not exhaustively queried, so extremely subtle journal exposure paths cannot be fully ruled out.

Only two sudo test invocations were captured before and one after reboot; broader/longer-running validation of the logging path under varied sudo usage (e.g., interactive sessions, sudo -i) was not captured.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command sequence is mostly clean: a first draft sudoers file with an extra iolog_dir option (cmd-21b2ef11308f48a9) was written only to /tmp and superseded by a corrected version before installation (cmd-da586375f14c40f5), so it caused no persisted residue. Temporary test artifacts (/tmp/sudo-log-test-file and the staging /tmp/sudo-command-logging file) were explicitly removed (cmd-72f070e9f567403e). The only residue found is /tmp/reboot.log, created as a redirection target for the background 'shutdown -r now' command (cmd-1991cd80cbcc4e44) and still present in the after-executor temp-file snapshot; it is small, low-risk, and a direct byproduct of the required restart-evidence step, but it was not cleaned up. No failed services, no unsafe exposure changes, and package health remained consistent before and after.
